notes: All nutrients, when you want them: a button on the back of every card, and "All nutrients for the day" in Progress. Energy, protein, carbohydrate, sugar, total, saturated, mono- and polyunsaturated fat, cholesterol, plant sterols, fibre (total, soluble, beta-glucan) and sodium, with your limits where there are any.
Scanning a pack now keeps its protein, carbohydrate, sugar, fat, cholesterol and plant sterols too.
Cards and day scores now use the numbers from packs you've scanned, the same as the planner does.
Filling in a day has a Done button.

Fill in a day you missed: Progress › tap yesterday or the day before › Fill in what you had. Log each meal (the planned one, another from the list, something else, or skipped), supper, the tablet, a walk and extras.
The bell reminds you when yesterday's meals aren't logged, and quietly drops it once they are.
Meals you log after the fact come out of the pantry, and that day's score updates.
Importing an order no longer takes apple juice for an apple, or egg noodles for an egg. Products that only contain a food's name are left on Skip, with a hint, until you pick them.
Import an order (Pantry): screenshot your Sixty60 cart or paste its text. Each item is read with its pack size, quantity and price, matched to your foods, and added to the pantry in one tap.
A tin's printed weight becomes its drained weight for tinned fish and beans, so a 170 g tuna tin counts as about 120 g of fish.
Prices from the order replace the rough estimates in your shopping total.
Scan a label tries again on its own. If energy, saturated fat or sodium is missing, it looks at the photo another way, up to three times, and keeps what each try read.
A read that doesn't add up (energy against the protein, carbohydrate and fat beside it) is called out instead of trusted, and a lost decimal point (174 for 17.4) is put back.
If a number still can't be read, it says which one.
Scan another side: a pack's table and its weight are often on different sides. Scan both and the numbers add up, with nothing read overwritten.
Mark a food as needing a rinse. Meals with it start with a rinse step, the pantry tags it, and the shopping list suggests a no-rinse one next time.
Energy printed as "Energy (kJ) 359" is read and converted, and drained tables are called out.
Pulling down on a sheet's contents now scrolls it instead of closing it. Drag the grey handle to close.
Scan a label reads energy when it's printed in the heading, like "Energy (kJ) 359", and tells you when the table is for the drained food.
What's new is sorted: this update on top, older changes folded under their day.
Scan a label opens without the keyboard jumping up and shifting the sheet.
Lemon is now Lemon juice (a 250 g bottle, in the flavour aisle), and tips that needed zest are changed to match.
Add a food that isn't in the list from its label (Pantry › Scan a label, or the big plus), also from inside your own meal.
Type any pack size when you restock or add to the list. It starts from the size you last bought.
A scan can save the pack size, the price and how many packs to add to the pantry, all in one go.
A firm press no longer selects text or raises the iOS callout. Held sideways, the app asks you to turn it upright.
Nutrition figures are marked as estimates, with a plain explanation of where they come from (Me › This app, or the back of any card).
Bigger back buttons, and small touches in Me: sliding selections, a pop on ticks and values, screens that slide in.
Set when you eat under Me › Meal times. The cards and the snack reminder follow.
Me is big buttons for each area: About you, Medication, Menu and cards, Back up, This app.
Add or change your medication under Me › Medication.
See what's coming: dots under the cards bring lunch or the snack to the top.
The menu's buttons respond as you hold and slide your thumb. Pick a feel under Me › Menu feel.
A notification bell, top right: updates, new meals, tomorrow's shopping, low items, refills and reminders in one place.
Today is quieter: slimmer Tablet and Walk chips, and explanations only when they matter.
When daytime is done, Today looks ahead: tonight's prep, what to pick up for tomorrow, and tomorrow's meals.
Tell the app what supper is tonight and tomorrow's first question is already answered.
Me shows the version, with Check for updates and What's new.
Progress tab with blood results, and new meals to try as they arrive.
Had something else, and + Extra, when a meal didn't go to plan.
Add your own meal, scan a nutrition label, and a doctor summary you can share.
A Sunday look-back and a gentle backup reminder.
